newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa reaches pay deal with one union.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa reaches pay deal with one union.

text.p: Germany airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG reached a pay deal with one of its two unions on Friday, the public sector OeTV union said.

The OeTV said it had accepted Lufthansa's offer of a wage contract through to the end of 1998, giving workers one-off payments to cover the period until March 30 1998 and then a 1.7 percent wage rise.
Workers would receive one third of their monthly salary plus a bonus of 500 marks in a profit-sharing scheme to cover the initial period.

The deal with the OeTV, struck in the early hours of Friday morning, follows the collapse of negotations between the airline and the white collar union DAG on Thursday afternoon, with whom Lufthansa traditionally holds separate talks.
The leader of DAG's negotiating team Michael Tarp told Reuters that an offer Lufthansa had made on Wednesday was unacceptable, and would have left workers with wage rises below the rate of inflation.
A spokeswoman for Lufthansa said the airline had never before struck separate deals with its unions.
